sector_model: semicap metrology: P/E GAAP and guided, EV/sales, FCF yield after SBC, net cash after convertible
thesis: Nova Ltd. (Nasdaq: NVMI; Israel based foreign private issuer reporting US GAAP USD on 6-K/20-F) sells process control metrology to chipmakers. Q3 2026 revenue 287.8M (+28% y/y, +13% q/q), GAAP net income 90.0M (EPS 2.64), GAAP gross margin 57.7%, OCF 138.1M; Q4 guide revenue 305-315M and GAAP EPS 2.78-2.93. Cash, deposits and securities about 1.79B against 734.6M convertible notes (net cash about 1,055M). TTM revenue 1,001M, GAAP NI 299M, FCF 255M (capex 24.7M). At 327.64 (2026-11-12 close; 52-week range 266.43-615.99): market cap about 10.4B on 31.78M shares (approximation), EV about 9.4B, 9.4x TTM sales, 35x TTM GAAP earnings, about 29x annualized Q4 guided GAAP EPS, FCF yield 2.4%. Strong growth and balance sheet; valuation is full but far below PLTR; mispricing not demonstrated.
counterthesis: Semicap metrology is cyclical and concentrated: a few large customers, China and export-control exposure, and a stock that fell 47% from its high shows how fast sentiment turns (a drop from a high is not proof of cheapness). The Q3 jump in OCF may reflect working capital; convertible notes of 734.6M add dilution (diluted weighted shares 34.4M vs 31.8M basic); the share count used is a year-end approximation. Israeli operations add geopolitical risk. Peers, convertible terms, 20-F risk factors and notes unread.
invalidation: Thesis fails if quarterly revenue growth turns negative, gross margin falls below 55%, or advanced packaging and memory orders cancel. Valuation case needs P/E on guided GAAP EPS below about 20x or FCF yield above 5%.
